findings.title: Function Registry records incorrect security/search_path metadata
findings.detail: 128 security mismatches and 157 search_path mismatches. Registry parser uses an absolute match offset against a sliced function segment, so attributes are not parsed.

findings.title: Response-loss replay vector remains hardcoded
findings.detail: validate_r5.py assigns 'GENERATION:2' directly and compares the same stored string. It does not derive a first-execution result from the final SQL state transition or Ledger contract.

findings.title: Candidate backfill actor fields are not bound to the executing session
findings.detail: The SECURITY DEFINER function accepts arbitrary Principal, Session and Authority Grant IDs and only checks that those rows are active. It does not compare them with session_user, a locked current session, or backend identity. PUBLIC EXECUTE is revoked, so the current state is fail-closed, but any future maintenance grant could attribute immutable-row changes to another valid actor.

findings.title: R5 Validator contains non-mutational negative checks and a non-exact Open Decision check
findings.detail: Most IND-MUT rows in VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_R5 contain only a boolean predicate and basis text, without a target mutation, expected mutation effect, or observed flipped result. The Open Decisions check accepts at least 57 regex matches and does not itself require exactly 57 unique OPEN IDs with zero approvals.

findings.title: Documented R5 state-vector IDs do not resolve to evidence IDs
Begin samples authoritative time before the final active-Attempt lock
findings.detail: The R5 design document says locking precedes time evaluation. The final SQL samples clock_timestamp() before SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the active Attempt. The shared identity mutex currently serializes public writers, so no confirmed exploitation path was found, but the claimed lock/time order is false and owner DML or a future lock-order change could preserve a stale time decision.
